title: Mixed grazing maintains the spatial invariability of alpine grassland biomass by fostering a more diversified community structure and spatial heterogeneity
content:
Our results show that mixed grazing, by integrating a variety of herbivore foraging strategies, may eliminate the disproportionate role of dominant species on community spatial invariability of biomass. These findings underscore the critical role of mixed grazing in improving the community spatial invariability of biomass in alpine grasslands. Such integrated management practices can be crucial to maintaining the long-term functionality and stability of alpine grasslands, providing valuable insights for grassland conservation and sustainable grazing management.


Abstract

Grazing by large herbivores is widely recognized as an important driver of plant diversity, function and community stability (invariability) in grassland ecosystems. However, previous studies have focused primarily on the community temporal invariability of biomass under single herbivore grazing regimes. Since different herbivores have different foraging strategies, we hypothesize that mixed grazing can increase grassland heterogeneity and community spatial invariability of biomass. Using a 3-year field experiment in an alpine grassland implementing moderate grazing (medium grazing intensity) across various grazing types (including yaks grazing, sheep grazing and mixed grazing), we quantified the impact of different grazing types on the community spatial invariability of biomass and underlying processes including spatial covariation and invariability at the species level. We found that moderate grazing increased the community spatial invariability of biomass by reducing species-level spatial covariation. Furthermore, single grazing indirectly promoted community spatial invariability of biomass by increasing the spatial invariability of dominant species. Specifically, yaks grazing achieved this by suppressing species spatial covariation and improving species spatial invariability, while sheep grazing contributed primarily by improving species spatial invariability. On the contrary, mixed grazing improved the community spatial invariability of biomass by regulating species-level spatial covariation and invariability, independent of the influence of the dominant species. These results suggest that mixed grazing may diminish the disproportionate role of dominant species fostering multi-dominant species coexistence and greater spatial heterogeneity through the diverse behaviours of large herbivores. Synthesis and applications. Our study underscores the critical role of mixed grazing in improving the community spatial invariability of biomass in alpine grasslands. Our research reveals that yaks, sheep and mixed grazing under moderate intensity consistently improve spatial stability by reducing species-level spatial covariation. These findings highlight that mixed grazing, by integrating a variety of herbivore foraging strategies, not only increases the community spatial invariability of biomass but also promotes a resilient, heterogeneous ecosystem structure. Such integrated management practices can be crucial to maintaining the long-term functionality and stability of alpine grasslands, providing valuable insights for grassland conservation and sustainable grazing management.

抽象的

食草动物放牧是草地生态系统维持植物多样性、功能以及群落稳定性的重要驱动因素。以往研究主要聚焦于单一食草动物放牧对群落生物量时间稳定性的影响。鉴于牦牛和藏羊不同的采食策略，我们假设牦牛和藏羊混合放牧能够增加草地的空间异质性，并能提高群落生物量的空间不变性。 本研究在高寒草地上进行了一项为期三年的放牧实验，设置了中等放牧强度(即适度放牧)下不同放牧方式(包括牦牛放牧、绵羊放牧和牛羊混合放牧)，量化了不同放牧方式对高寒草地群落生物量空间稳定性的影响，并分析了不同放牧方式对物种水平的空间协变性和空间不变性的潜在作用过程。 适度放牧通过降低物种间的空间协变性，提高了群落生物量的空间稳定性。单一放牧通过增强优势种的空间不变性，间接促进了群落生物量的空间稳定性。牦牛放牧通过同时降低物种的空间协变性和提高物种的空间稳定性来实现这一效应；藏羊放牧则主要通过提升物种的空间稳定性来维持群落生物量的空间稳定性。而牦牛和藏羊混合放牧对群落空间稳定性的促进作用并不依赖于优势种，而是通过直接调节物种水平的空间协变性和空间稳定性来维持群落生物量的空间稳定性。这些结果表明，牦牛和藏羊混合放牧可借助不同采食行为的互补性，削弱单一优势种的主导作用，从而促进高寒草地群落的多优势种共存和更大的空间异质性。 综合与应用:本研究强调了牦牛和藏羊混合放牧在提升高寒草地群落生物量空间稳定性方面的关键作用。尽管所有放牧类型都能通过减少物种水平的空间协变来直接提高群落生物量的空间稳定性，但混合放牧的效果最为显著。具体而言，通过混合放牧不仅提高了群落生物量的空间稳定性，还有助于构建更具恢复力和多样性的生态系统结构。混合放牧对于维持高寒草地生态功能和稳定性至关重要。
